messages.subject: ploting raw data
parts:
Sorry if this is a silly question. How can you plot raw just raw data (7days, at 100hz) and not epoch 1 or 5 sec time series etc. The bin files created by geneactive are too large to open in excel for 7 days worth of data at 100hz. Is there a way to just work with the raw data manually with in R

thanks in advance

Adam

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] ploting raw data
parts:
Most computers would struggle to put all that data in memory and your screen will probably not have enough pixels to display all those numbers. This was one of the reasons why I developed GGIR: it loads and processes segments of the data and combines the results at the end to minimize memory requirements.
If you are keen to work with (segments of) the raw data directly then see package GENEAread.
Plotting of raw data in R is a lot quicker if you use argument type ="l" rather than the default type = "p".
Vincent
